sentences: PlanRace is a proposed Bittensor market for verified query optimization.
Miners discover executable index plans. Validators check the results on hidden workloads.
This interim pitch presents verified localnet evidence. Public testnet deployment remains pending.
A query can remain correct while becoming expensive as data and workloads change.
Our proposed first users are database teams investigating recurring performance regressions.
Centralized advisors offer strong integration. PlanRace explores whether independent solvers can find useful alternatives under a shared evaluation policy.
Buyer demand remains a hypothesis, not a customer result.
The commodity is a bounded structured index plan for a known correct query.
Miners can use search, learned systems, rules, or engine expertise.
They receive public training information and a resource budget. They cannot submit arbitrary executable code or their own timing claims.
Validators own the hidden fixtures and replay each artifact.
A cryptographic commitment binds each task to its hidden fixtures, engine, policy, and deadline.
Requests bind the intended receiver. Miner signatures bind submitted artifacts.
After the deadline, the validator seals submissions and reveals the secret seed and salt.
Auditors can then regenerate the fixtures and verify the commitment.
Exact results and policy compliance come before performance.
Passing candidates face the same baseline across cold and warm latency, setup cost, storage, and reuse horizons.
The protocol aggregates conservative measurements across workload families and epochs.
An all-fail round makes no new weight update. It does not clear old on-chain weights.
The committed simulation ran five hundred twelve seeded adversarial replications.
It recorded zero false acceptance and zero exact-copy allocation gain in those tested cases.
A material limitation remains: behavior-equivalent replicas improved availability, with a worst allocation gain of thirteen point five seven percentage points.
This is bounded simulation evidence, not a universal Sybil-resistance proof.
The verified local Subtensor run covered thirty epochs and six query families.
Three validator identities under one operator queried ten heterogeneous miners.
The run recorded three hundred authenticated requests and two hundred seventy signed responses, with finalized local-chain weight readback.
These are localnet results. They do not demonstrate a public testnet deployment.
Bittensor can coordinate an open population of competing optimization strategies.
PlanRace separates open-ended discovery from bounded validator replay.
Cheaper verification is an economic hypothesis that must hold as workloads scale.
Disposable workers bound evaluation resources. Independent operators, hardware calibration, and real buyer workloads still require validation.
The next proof gate is a dedicated public testnet run with registered miners and validators.
It must produce signed interaction, scoring, finalized weights, and a matching public metagraph readback.
Test token funding remains outstanding.
Later work targets independent validators and production database adapters. Current evidence uses generated SQLite workloads and does not prove private-data safety or commercial demand.
PlanRace has a working local mechanism and public, auditable evidence.
HackQuest accepted the project submission with its testnet-pending status disclosed.
The public repository and dashboard contain the implementation and its limitations.
This interim pitch does not replace the required testnet demo. The final result section will change only when real chain evidence exists.
